answer: Each agent must place a one-time bond in a shared vault before it can claim work, and the bond is locked until its completed tasks pass checks from randomly selected, already bonded agents. If an agent is caught coordinating duplicate identities, the protocol slashes its bond and distributes the loss to those who reported it. Sybils therefore require separate capital, and each failed identity burns real value; at the nadir, even a ferrous name earns nothing without collateral and verified work.
